b1.model_change: Ingestion silently censors top 5% (quantile guard). Censored Exp mean = s*(1-e^-q(q/s+1))/0.95 -> 0.837*2.75=2.30, matches observed. Revised model: mean of UNCENSORED data = 2.75; pipeline must drop the outlier guard for heavy-tailed data.

c1.model_change: Trial runner reseeds RNG with a constant inside the loop -> all 1000 trials identical -> zero variance. Fix: seed once outside loop. Revised prediction restores sd(single max)/sqrt(100).

c2.model_change: mean() uses integer floor division (sum // n), flooring 10.5 to 10.0. Fix: true division. Hypothesis itself was correct.

c3.model_change: total_return() slices xs[:n//2], summing only half the series (obs 2.91 ~ n/2*mu). Fix: sum full series -> n*mu = 5.92.

d1.model_change: central_tendency_mean() returns the MEDIAN. For LogNormal, median = exp(mu) = 3.10 (matches obs 3.16), mean = exp(mu+sigma^2/2) = 4.77. The metric, not the hypothesis, was wrong. Fix: use arithmetic mean.

d3.model_change: average() is a 10% two-sided trimmed mean. Exponential is right-skewed, so trimming removes more mass from the top -> 1.67 < 2.0. Untrimmed mean = 2.0. Fix: report trimming explicitly or use full mean.

e3.model_change: My frame treated prevalence as fixable by assumption (2%). PPV is undefined without the base rate - it is a two-parameter question I compressed into one. With revealed prevalence 0.037: PPV = 0.95*0.037/(0.95*0.037+0.05*0.963) = 0.422. Revised concept set: always carry prevalence as an explicit variable.
